Subject: Preflight: traffic census & workload sampling for Dedicated commitment (Pinnacle)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for taking time last week. We’re preparing to evaluate a Dedicated capacity commitment and want to get ahead on the sizing side so procurement can move faster. I’ve attached a 48-hour token-sampled CSV from production (anonymized) — it contains timestamps, endpoint, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and session_id.

High-level context:
- Primary workload: conversational customer support (mix of short clarifications and longer summarizations)
- Peak window: 11:00–14:00 PT, sustained for ~90 minutes, with spikes to ~3.2k concurrent sessions
- Current model: open-source 13B fine-tuned; we plan to test a quantized 13B variant on your Dedicated fleet

Before we schedule a deeper technical session, could you send your pre-sales traffic census or a short questionnaire we can fill? Specifically we need:
- Suggested fields/prompt samples you need for accurate sizing
- Any minimum sample window you recommend
- What metrics influence the SKU recommendation (e.g., p99 token latency, parallel KV memory per session)

Attaching: pinnacle_traffic_sample.csv (anonymized).

Appreciate it — want to make sure procurement has everything by next Tuesday.

—Sara
Sara Wright
Head of Infrastructure, Pinnacle Analytics
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

Hi Sara — thanks for the sample and context. Attached is our preflight questionnaire (redwood_preflight_questionnaire_v2.xlsx) — it’s a compact form that maps directly to our Dedicated sizing heuristics. Quick notes before you jump in:

- Please include representative prompt-response pairs where possible (we use these to estimate KV cache utilization and average token per request).
- If you have labeled high/low criticality routes (e.g., billing, login-verification), mark them — we recommend different SLOs for critical routes.
- For sustained concurrency, list both session concurrency and API concurrency if you use session pooling.

A couple of clarifying questions for our sizing team:
- Is the 3.2k concurrent sessions figure a hard peak or a bursty instantaneous spike? If bursty, what’s the 95th–99th percentile window?
- Do you have an SLA target for p99 generation latency? Many customers choose 500–800ms p99 for interactive features; we can recommend different SKUs based on that.

I’ve looped in Karthik (serving runtime) and Marissa (dedicated capacity planning) so we can triage any follow-ups once you return the questionnaire. If you prefer, we can do a 30-min tech intake tomorrow afternoon.

Next steps / ask:
- Fill the attached questionnaire and send it back by EOD Monday (7/10) OR book a 30-min intake: https://cal.redwood/tessa/30

Best,
Tessa Morgan

Hi Sara — quick technical primer / things that help our sizing algorithm: 

On Fri, Jul 8, 2028 at 9:14 AM Sara Wright <sara.wright@pinnacleanalytics.com> wrote:
> (attached: pinnacle_traffic_sample.csv)

Thanks for the sample — a few concrete asks so we can avoid back-and-forth:
1) Prompt/response length distribution: if you can provide a short histogram or typical buckets (0–64, 65–256, 257–1024, 1025+ tokens) that’s ideal. We can infer, but explicit buckets speed up SKU mapping.
2) Session affinity details: are your sessions single-turn or multi-turn long-lived with KV reuse? If multi-turn, include average KV cache size per session (or approximate average context length).
3) Tokenization note: indicate whether tokens are GPT-token-like or a custom tokenizer (we assume GPT-like by default).
4) Peak vs sustained: give us both peak concurrent API connections (instantaneous) and sustained concurrency (5–15 minute average).

For initial sizing we’ll run two scenario paths:
- conservative (p99 latency target = 500ms, smaller SKUs with more nodes)
- aggressive (p99 latency target = 800ms, fewer larger SKUs)

If you’re open, please include any monthly commit target range (e.g., 1–5M tokens/day) — that helps determine whether Dedicated Reserved or hybrid (dedicated + burst on hosted) is a better economic fit.

Happy to take the intake call and walk through the questionnaire — I can run a quick projection live.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik / Tessa — thanks. Quick answers inline: 

On Sat, Jul 9, 2028 at 9:30 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 1) Prompt/response length distribution
We pulled basic buckets from the sample: ~48% 0–64 tokens, ~32% 65–256, ~17% 257–1024, ~3% >1024. Avg prompt_tokens = 42; avg completion_tokens = 160.

> 2) Session affinity
Majority are short-lived (single session per user) but we have a 12% population of multi-turn sessions (avg of 6 turns, reuse KV). Average KV footprint for multi-turn = ~12MB per session (anonymized estimate).

> 3) Tokenization
We use a GPT-like tokenizer (standard).

> 4) Peak vs sustained
Peak instantaneous API connections: 3,200
Sustained (10-min avg during peak window): 950

Procurement also attached an initial SLA/contract ask — see sla-draft-v1.pdf. They want a draft so legal can internalize latency/availability objectives early.

We’ll fill the questionnaire today and return it — thanks for the quick guidance. Can you also confirm whether Redwood recommends quantized int8 variants for this workload and any expected throughput penalties?

—Sara

Hi Sara — great, thanks for the buckets and the quick turnaround on the questionnaire. Summary & next steps from our side: 

Summary (what we heard):
- Workload: conversational support; avg request ~200 tokens total; ~12% multi-turn with ~12MB KV reuse
- Peak: instantaneous 3.2k API connections; 10-min sustained ~950
- Tokenization: GPT-like

Redwood recommended starter:
- Technical SKU path: 8x A100S + NVLink (or equivalent 80GB-class instances) as baseline for conservative p99=500ms sizing; alternate path: 4x 80GB nodes with aggressive packing targeting p99=800ms.
- Quantization: int8 recommended for cost parity; expect ~10–18% throughput drop vs float16 depending on kernel and prompt shapes — Karthik will model exact token/s latency trade-offs in the intake call.

Action items / owners:
- Pinnacle: return questionnaire + any labeled prompt samples (Sara) — target: EOD 7/11
- Redwood (Karthik): run two sizing projections (conservative/aggressive) and produce a short SKU comparison doc — ETA: 7/12
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare Dedicated cost estimate + reserve commitment options for DEAL-2028-PIN-0042 — ETA: 7/13
- Mutual: schedule 30-min technical intake if outstanding questions (Tessa to send calendar link)

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.redwood/deal/DEAL-2028-PIN-0042) and shared questionnaire (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPinnaclePreflight).

If that looks good, we’ll lock the intake slot for Wednesday and I’ll have the projected SKU comparison in advance.
